_authors_note: 2026-10-22 design simplification (PI): one authoring agent, m0 = Claude Code with claude-fable-5-1. The codex mode m1 (gpt-6.1-sol) was retired before the seal; its attempts remain under authored/ as history and enter no analysis. The approach is model-agnostic; a second agent (Qwen2.5-72B on the VHPC cluster) is a planned extension, not part of this run.
_env_note: env (corpus/envs.py): one environment per base commit, shared by commits whose dependency files are identical; battery_cmd names its interpreter with {python}. The install steps follow the commit's own manifests: requirements/tests.txt until flask switched to uv in May 2025 (0109e496, which removed it and added uv.lock), the tests dependency group after; a base commit with neither (setup.py only, before eea31f29 added requirements/tests.txt on 2020-05-23) has no environment, and pairs records it as not admitted. exclude_newer dependency-change resolves the steps as of the last commit that changed a dependency file, so the unpinned Werkzeug and click take that date's releases: at the January 2024 base of flask-5377 today's click 8.5 fails three CLI tests (CliRunner(mix_stderr=...) is gone) and click 8.1.7 passes. The tools are the study's pins, installed last and without the cutoff. atheris 2.2.2 is the newest release with a macOS arm64 Python 3.10 wheel (2.3.0 and later ship only an sdist there, which needs a libFuzzer clang). host_tools pins the two tools that run outside the environment: semgrep, which F2 runs from a venv of its own (corpus.envs.ensure_tool), because semgrep 1.181.0 requires click~=8.4.2 and would move the subject's click in either direction; and hypothesis, which generates and shrinks ch.property's inputs in the orchestrator (requirements-dev.txt pins the same version; the environment's copy serves only code that runs in the subject's interpreter). Under a freeze record evidence.run refuses either at another version.
_oracle_note: oracle_cmd is the hidden injecting oracle (corpus.oracle; Sec. sec:pool, RQ1 setup spec Secs. 5-6): {python} is the base commit's interpreter, {candidate} the candidate id and {mode} battery for admission (a) or catch for (b), filled per candidate by corpus.build pairs; exit 0 means passed or caught, and every run writes corpus/<repo>/oracle/<candidate_id>.json. Admission (a) is battery_cmd, the repository's own suite under the base commit's interpreter (CI's half), and then the hidden battery on the safe variant: oracle_battery (oracle/<repo>/test_battery_*.py below the shared oracle/conftest.py, kept outside the checkout) plus the gold patch's added or modified tests under tests_dir (base_commit..merge_commit, read from the clone's history), evaluated differentially, so a battery test failing at the base commit is excluded for that candidate and listed in the admission row's battery_excluded, never a rejection, and a failing gold test rejects with its own reason, gold_tests_fail. Admission (b) is the battery failing on the unsafe twin where it passes on the safe one, or the AST scanner (corpus.oracle_scanner, disjoint from F2's rules) flagging the seeded site, or twin differential execution of the battery's observations diverging; the row's caught_by names which. Nothing of the oracle is ever written into the checkout or reaches a producer's Context.

The same out as configs/flask-tune.json (m0, m1), so the three arms sit together for the within-task comparison; a separate config and record so each arm's fingerprint stays valid for the whole of its run.
